issues.description: Developer instance method name mismatch: the problem statement and the template declare and document an instance method named attend(course:) for the Developer class, but the solution implementation defines a method named participateIn(course:). The solution's Client calls myself.attend(course:), so the mismatched method name in the solution will cause a compilation error and confuses students about the intended API. Files and locations: problem_statement.md (task description of attend) expects attend(course:) (lines 43-47); the template stub declares func attend(course: Course?) in Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift (line 34); the solution implementation declares func participateIn(course: Course?) in Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift (signature at line 42); the solution's client calls myself.attend(course:) in Sources/DeveloperLib/Client.swift (line 19).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the instance method name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's participateIn(course:) method to attend(course:) with signature func attend(course: Course?) so it matches the problem statement, the template stub, and the Client call. Alternatively (less preferred), update the problem statement, template, and Client to use participateIn(course:). Ensure the implementation preserves the specified behavior: optional-binding, checking course.name.lowercased().contains("swift"), incrementing or setting monthsOfSwiftExperience, and printing the success message.
